Class ScreenPanelRegistry

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.ScreenPanelRegistry
@Internal public final class ScreenPanelRegistry extends Object
Library-owned registry of MenuContext ScreenPanelAdapters that declare targeting via .on(...) or .onAny(). Listens once on ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT and dispatches render/input to the adapters whose targeting matches each opened AbstractContainerScreen. Consumers stop writing per-screen ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT boilerplate — the library owns the hook.

See menukit/Design Docs/Phase 12.5/M8_FOUR_CONTEXT_MODEL.md §8 for the design and §7.3 for orphan-adapter enforcement.

Adapter lifecycle

  1. Construction. new ScreenPanelAdapter(panel, region) calls trackPending(ScreenPanelAdapter) — the adapter joins PENDING until it declares targeting.
  2. Targeting declaration. .on(Class...) or .onAny() calls markTargetingDeclared(ScreenPanelAdapter) — the adapter moves from PENDING to REGISTERED.
  3. Default checkpoint. On the first screen-open event after init, applyEverywhereDefault() runs. Any adapter still in PENDING declared no targeting, so it defaults to every container screen — the uniform "default-on, opt-out" model shared with MKCContainerPanel. Narrow it deliberately with .on(...) / .onPlayerInventory() / .onMatching(allExcept(...)).
  4. Dispatch. For each opened AbstractContainerScreen, walk REGISTERED and for adapters whose targeting matches the screen class, cache the match list in SCREEN_DATA and register a ScreenMouseEvents.allowMouseClick hook. Render dispatch runs via MKPanelRenderMixin (injects at INVOKE renderCarriedItem so panels land in the right render stratum — see M8 §8.2 for why Fabric's afterRender is the wrong hook for render). Fabric handles per-screen click-hook lifetime cleanup when the screen closes.

    • init

      public static void init()
      Registers the library-owned ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT listener. Called once from MKClient.onInitializeClient. After this, any region-based adapter that declared targeting will render on matching screens without the consumer writing per-screen boilerplate.

    • renderMatchingPanels

      public static void renderMatchingPanels(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, int mouseX, int mouseY)
      Called from MKPanelRenderMixin at the injection point in AbstractContainerScreen.render (before renderCarriedItem). Dispatches all matching MenuContext and SlotGroupContext adapters for the current screen. No-op for screens with no matches, or for screens opened before onScreenInit(Minecraft, Screen, int, int) populated the cache (shouldn't happen in practice — AFTER_INIT fires before the first render).

      Public visibility required because the mixin is in a different package (mixin) from this class (inject).

    • shouldEatCovered

      public static boolean shouldEatCovered(boolean covered)
      M9 pure decision used by the allowMouseClick hook to determine whether a click should be eaten from vanilla.

      Returns true when the cursor is inside any visible opaque panel's bounds — vanilla shouldn't see the click since the panel is sitting opaquely over the coords. Returns false otherwise.

      Extracted from the click-hook closure so /mkverify probes can test the decision without instantiating a screen.

    • dispatchCoveredClick

      public static boolean dispatchCoveredClick(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      M9 opaque click dispatch — combined dispatch + eat decision called from MKModalMouseHandlerMixin at the HEAD of MouseHandler.onButton. Fires before any per-Screen routing so subclass-specific click handling (creative-mode tabs, etc.) doesn't pre-empt the opacity decision.

      Decision tree:

      • Click inside any visible opaque panel — dispatches to that panel's adapter (so its element layer gets the click), returns true to signal eat. Vanilla never sees the click.
      • Click outside all opaque panels + a tracksAsModal panel visible — returns true (eat) without dispatching. Modal-tracking blocks underlying interaction outside its bounds (preserves 14d-1 modal semantics).
      • Click outside all opaque panels + no tracksAsModal panel — returns false; vanilla dispatch proceeds and the Fabric allowMouseClick hook handles non-modal region-based click dispatch normally.

      Successor to 14d-1's dispatchModalClick, generalized for non-modal opaque panels. Same atomic-dispatch-and-eat shape.

    • dispatchCoveredRelease

      public static boolean dispatchCoveredRelease(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      M9 opaque release dispatch — symmetric counterpart to dispatchCoveredClick(Screen, double, double, int). Called from MKModalMouseHandlerMixin.onButton when action == 0 (GLFW_RELEASE).

      Why this exists (smoke fold-inline finding): Initial M9 implementation passed releases through unconditionally (let Fabric allowMouseRelease handle drag-end for ScrollContainer). That broke modal blocking for vanilla release-driven UIs: CreativeModeInventoryScreen.mouseReleased is what selects creative tabs (not mouseClicked), so passed-through releases switched tabs while a modal was visible.

      Symmetric handling: when the press would have been eaten (opaque at cursor OR modal-tracking visible), eat the release too. Since eating cancels the entire MouseHandler.onButton chain, Fabric's allowMouseRelease hook can't fire — so this method also manually dispatches adapter.mouseReleased to all visible opaque adapters' elements (drag-end semantic preserved).

      Decision tree:

      • Cursor inside any visible opaque panel — eat at mixin level; manually dispatch mouseReleased to all visible opaque adapters so any in-progress drag (on a ScrollContainer or future draggable element) ends.
      • Cursor outside opaque + tracksAsModal panel visible — eat at mixin level (modal blocks tab selection on release). Still dispatch mouseReleased to opaque adapters in case a drag started inside an opaque panel and cursor moved outside before release.
      • No opaque + no modal-tracking — return false (don't eat); release passes through to vanilla → Fabric allowMouseRelease → adapter.mouseReleased dispatch (existing 14d-2 plumbing).

    • dispatchCoveredScroll

      public static boolean dispatchCoveredScroll(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY, double scrollX, double scrollY)
      M9 opaque scroll dispatch — parallels dispatchCoveredClick(Screen, double, double, int). Called from MKModalMouseHandlerMixin.onScroll at the HEAD of MouseHandler.onScroll.

      Cursor inside an opaque panel: dispatch scroll to its elements; return true. Cursor outside + tracksAsModal visible: eat without dispatch. Cursor outside + no modal-tracking: pass through.

    • findCoveringPanelAt

      public static @Nullable ScreenPanelAdapter findCoveringPanelAt(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Unified coverage query — finds the topmost (last-registered) visible panel that claims the cursor point (panelClaimsPoint(Panel, ScreenOrigin, int, double, double): an opaque background minus holes, OR a solid opaque element). Iterates region adapters (via SCREEN_DATA) so they participate in the click-through prohibition.

      Iteration order: registration order. Highest-z = last-registered wins; iterate forward and overwrite.

      This is the dispatch-returning half of the inertness contract (it returns the panel so the caller can route the input to its elements); the boolean half consumers/suppressors call is MKFocus.isInertUnderPanel(double, double).

      Returns:
      the topmost claiming adapter at coords, or null if none visible OR the cursor is over no panel's opaque background/element

    • hasActiveOverlayAt

      public static boolean hasActiveOverlayAt(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Post-Phase 18r-5: complement to anyPanelCoversPoint(double, double) for ELEMENT-LEVEL active overlays — Dropdown popovers and any other element whose getActiveOverlayBounds() extends beyond its owning panel's bounds. The panel-bounds query misses these; this query catches them.

      Used by the widget-hover-suppression mixin so vanilla widgets (buttons, list rows) covered by an open dropdown popover stop highlighting on hover. The opacity-eat input path already routes the CLICK away from them; this closes the visual loop.

    • applyEverywhereDefault

      public static void applyEverywhereDefault()
      Applies the everywhere-default to region-based adapters that reached the first screen-open without declaring targeting. An undeclared region-based ScreenPanelAdapter defaults to every container screen — the uniform "default-on, opt-out" model shared with MKCContainerPanel. A consumer narrows it deliberately with .on(...) / .onPlayerInventory() / .onMatching(ScreenMatcher.allExcept(...)).

      Runs on every screen-open after init (not just the first). Anything still in PENDING declared no targeting — whether it was built at init or constructed mid-session by a runtime toggle. Each is promoted via ScreenPanelAdapter.onAny() (sets the every-screen target and moves it PENDING → REGISTERED so dispatch picks it up). Idempotent: the method early-returns when PENDING is empty.

      Container screens only — non-container vanilla screens (Options, title, …) keep the explicit-targeting requirement in VanillaScreenPanelRegistry.validateTargetingDeclared(); an everywhere-default makes no sense there.
